fx.note: Model is built in AUD (the reporting currency of the ASX-primary-listed entity). Per-share outputs are converted to NZD at this rate for comparison with the NZX quote. current_price_aud = 45.17 / 1.1988 = 37.68 (cross-checked against the live ANZ.AX quote of A$37.73 -- a 5-cent difference consistent with the two listings trading a few minutes apart, not a data error). Rate re-verified live 2026-08-09 and unchanged from the 2026-08-08 run.

valuation_philosophy.rationale: ANZ Group Holdings is a leveraged deposit-taking bank. Operating cash flow and 'free cash flow' as conventionally defined are meaningless for a bank because customer deposits and wholesale funding movements dominate the cash flow statement and are funding activities, not operating cash generation available to equity holders. Net debt is likewise not a meaningful concept for a bank's balance sheet -- deposits and wholesale borrowings ARE the funding base for interest-earning assets, not a claim to be netted against enterprise value. This model instead follows the same approach used for SOFI and SRBK in this repository: project statutory NPAT/EPS, discount at the cost of equity (not WACC), and cap the terminal value at the lower of a Gordon Growth perpetuity (applied to the year-5 EPS, i.e. the earnings-power base, consistent with the exit-P/E cap which is also EPS-based) and an exit-P/E multiple anchored to ANZ's own 10-year historical trading range. Explicit-period cash flows to equity holders are modelled as the dividend actually paid out (EPS x payout ratio); the terminal value capitalizes the full earnings stream because retained earnings continue to compound book value and back future distributions beyond the explicit window. A dividend-discount cross-check is provided as a memo. Entry price uses the same earnings/dividend framework at a 15% hurdle rate rather than the FCF-and-net-debt formula used for non-financial companies.
valuation_philosophy.sbc_note: Stock-based compensation is immaterial for ANZ (a large regulated bank paying primarily cash salaries/bonuses with modest deferred equity awards) and is not separately modelled. Share count is held roughly flat to slightly declining in the base/bull cases, reflecting the historical on-market buyback pattern (though the remaining on-market buyback programme has been ceased since H1-2026 pending capital build and APRA remediation funding -- see buyback_status). The bear case grows share count modestly on the assumption capital pressure forces occasional DRP-driven issuance instead.
valuation_philosophy.net_debt_note: Not applicable / not used. Deposits (~A$771bn at March 2026, up 3% half-on-half) and wholesale debt are funding for the loan book, not a net-debt overhang to subtract from enterprise value. No net-debt adjustment is made anywhere in this model.

inputs.fy2025_one_offs_note: FY2025 statutory NPAT of $6,035m was depressed by ~$250m ASIC/Federal Court conduct penalties (finalised December 2025, the largest combined ASIC penalty ever levied against a single entity) plus Suncorp integration and restructuring charges (cost-to-income rose to 58.2% cash from 51.3%). H1-2026 NPAT of $3,650m (cash profit up 6% YoY to $3,780m, up 14% ex significant items; cash ROTE up 161bps to 11.6%; cost-to-income cash improved to 49.4%) shows the trough clearing, but is not extrapolated at its annualized run-rate ($7,300m) as that would overstate a single half-year's momentum ahead of full Suncorp migration (34% complete at March 2026) and while the APRA $1bn operational-risk capital add-on remains a permanent drag.
inputs.sbc_source: not applicable -- immaterial for a bank; not separately modelled
inputs.buyback_status: H1-2026: remaining prior on-market buyback programme ceased; board prioritising capital build and CEU remediation funding over further buybacks near term. New since prior run: ANZ completed the buyout of Worldline's 51% stake in the ANZ Worldline merchant-payments JV for A$89m (July 2026), taking full ownership -- an immaterial cash outflow (~1.5% of one year's NPAT) relative to the balance sheet and not separately modelled in the projections, but noted as a small forward driver of Institutional/payments income (see growth_drivers).

historical_growth.notes: NPAT has been cyclical/flat over the trailing decade (FY2016 $5,709m to FY2025 $6,035m, a 10-year CAGR of only ~0.6%), with a FY2022-23 cyclical peak of ~$7.1-7.2bn on post-COVID margin expansion followed by FY2024-25 normalization and one-off conduct/restructuring charges. EPS CAGR is even weaker (~flat) because share count grew via the FY2022/Suncorp-era capital raise. This is why the DCF anchors to a mid-cycle NPAT level (~$6.5bn) with low single-digit forward growth rather than extrapolating either the FY2025 trough or the H1-2026 recovery rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (~2.2-2.8%) and NPAT CAGR (~0.6% over 10yr) are consistent with each other and with the low-single-digit growth used in the base case; no divergence flag required.

base.starting_npat_rationale: Mid-cycle NPAT, roughly the FY2021-25 five-year average ($6,615m) adjusted down slightly to exclude the FY2022-23 cyclical NIM-expansion peak, and above the FY2025 one-off-depressed actual ($6,035m).
base.exit_pe_rationale: Anchored to the 10-year average historical P/E of 13.27x (13.10x ex-FY2020 COVID trough), applying a modest discount for the ongoing APRA Court Enforceable Undertaking / remediation overhang (the $1bn operational-risk capital add-on, raised from $750m in Jan-2026, remains in force with no relief yet).

bull.starting_npat_rationale: Cost-out/2030 strategy (Suncorp synergies tracking ahead of the ~$500m p.a. target, FY2026 productivity savings guided ~$800-875m) delivers ahead of schedule; NPAT trends toward ~$7.5-8.1bn by year 5.

bear.starting_npat_rationale: NZ/AU margin compression continues (cash NIM already down to 1.53% in H1-2026 from 1.56%), NZ home-loan share loss to Kiwibank/ASB persists, credit cycle normalizes (impairment charge already up to 0.07% of average loans from 0.04%), remediation costs persist under continued APRA oversight; NPAT held flat near the FY2020-adjacent stress level, well below the FY2025 actual.

base.terminal_value_used_note: Gordon (applied to year-5 EPS as the earnings-power base) and the 12x exit-P/E cap coincide almost exactly at these assumptions (10.5% CoE, 2% terminal growth implies a ~11.8x perpetuity multiple, essentially equal to the 12x cap) -- both approaches agree the business is worth roughly 12x mature earnings.
base.implied_exit_multiple_vs_current_market_: Implied exit multiple (12.0x forward EPS) is below the current market-implied trailing P/E (~19.0x on FY2025 EPS), i.e. the model does NOT assume multiple expansion -- it assumes some de-rating back toward the 10-year historical average (13.27x).

dividend_discount_cross_check_memo.method: Simple one-stage Gordon growth on FY2025 DPS: DPS x (1+g) / (CoE - g)
dividend_discount_cross_check_memo.note: This crude single-stage DDM (no near-term growth phase, straight off the FY2025 dividend) lands close to the primary base-case IV of $23.52 AUD, corroborating the earnings-at-CoE result independently.

entry_price.method: Discount 5 years of base-case projected dividends per share plus a year-5 exit value (Y5 EPS x base-case exit-P/E of 12x) at the 15% hurdle rate, per share. No net-debt adjustment (not applicable for a bank).

sensitivity.note: Base-case NPAT/growth/payout/exit-multiple structure held constant; cost of equity and terminal growth varied. Several upper-left cells are flat because the 12x exit-P/E cap binds before Gordon growth would otherwise, capping intrinsic value even as CoE falls or terminal growth rises -- this is the terminal-value cap working as intended, not a calculation error.

probability_weighted.weighted_iv_note: weighted_iv duplicates weighted_iv_nzd so the cross-ticker screener compares like-for-like against current_price (NZ$45.17, the NZX quote). The model itself is built in AUD; weighted_iv_aud is the native-currency figure.

sanity_check.method: 10-year monthly close history re-fetched 2026-08-09 for the AUD-quoted line (ANZ.AX) via Yahoo Finance; each fiscal-year-end (30 Sep) close matched against that FY's EPS (cents->dollars) and book value per share (ShareholdersEquity / SharesOutstanding), both from ANZ.NZ_Metrics.csv (AUD reporting currency), so price and fundamentals are in the same currency throughout -- no FX conversion needed on this side. The current-price side (NZD, NZX quote) IS converted to AUD via the fx.audnzd rate for the implied-multiples comparison below; that conversion is cross-checked against the live ANZ.AX quote (A$37.73 direct vs A$37.68 via FX -- a 5-cent/0.1% difference, immaterial). SBC adjustment marked not applicable (immaterial for a bank, not separately modelled). EV/EBITDA and P/Sales marked null -- not meaningful metrics for a leveraged deposit-taking bank; P/E and P/B are the applicable multiples for a bank and are used instead.
sanity_check.ev_ebitda_note: Not meaningful for a bank -- EBITDA is not a coherent concept when interest income/expense is the core business (interest is operating revenue, not a financing cost to add back). Marked null rather than silently omitted.
sanity_check.p_sales_note: Not meaningful for a bank -- 'revenue' for a bank mixes net interest income (already a margin, not a top-line sales figure) with fee/trading income, so a Price/Sales multiple is not comparable to non-financial companies and is not used. P/E and P/B are the applicable multiples and are populated above instead.
sanity_check.sbc_adjustment_note: SBC is immaterial for ANZ and is not separately modelled; recorded here rather than silently omitted per workflow requirement.
sanity_check.diagnosis: Model output is well within ANZ's own 10-year historical trading range on both P/E (implied 11.87x vs range 10.22x-18.50x, average 13.27x) and P/B (implied 1.00x vs range 0.86x-1.56x, average 1.26x). No trip rules fired. The large negative headline upside (-37.6% base case) is not a sanity-check failure -- it reflects that the CURRENT market price sits near the top of ANZ's own historical multiple range (implied P/E ~19.0x, P/B ~1.61x, both above the 10-year average and P/E above even the 10-year max of 18.50x recorded at FY2025-end), driven by a strong 12-month rally (ANZ.AX roughly A$25 to A$37.7) on H1-2026 turnaround optimism. The model is flagging a valuation gap between a re-rated market price and mid-cycle earnings power, not producing an implausible output.
sanity_check.fix_applied: none -- sanity check passed, no adjustment required
sanity_check.market_context_note: The current market price (NZ$45.17, ~A$37.68) implies a much richer P/E of ~19.0x FY2025 EPS and P/B of ~1.61x -- both ABOVE the 10-year historical average (13.3x / 1.26x) and near or above the top of the 10-year range, reflecting the stock's strong rally over the past 12 months (ANZ.AX roughly $25 to $37.7 AUD-equivalent) on H1-2026 recovery optimism (cash profit +6% YoY, cash ROTE +161bps to 11.6%, cost-to-income cash improved to 49.4%) and the completed Worldline buyout. The DCF's base-case intrinsic value of A$23.52 (implied P/E 11.9x, P/B 1.0x) sits comfortably WITHIN the historical range, i.e. the model is not producing an implausible output -- it is flagging that the market is currently paying a premium to ANZ's own historical multiple range for the post-Matos turnaround thesis (Suncorp synergies, ANZ Plus rollout, cost-out) to play out in full, while the APRA CEU / $1bn capital add-on overhang and NZ mortgage-share losses remain unresolved. No sanity-check fix was required.
